newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson to upgrade Chilean mobile network.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson to upgrade Chilean mobile network.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group AB LM Ericsson said on Monday it won a contract with Startel in Chile to upgrade the country's largest D-AMPS mobile telephone network for Personal Communication Services (PCS).
Ericsson said the new digital services were being introduced initially in Santiago but would later be extended across the entire national network.
"The company expects digital subscribers to account for over ten percent of its subscriber base by the end 1997," Ericsson said in a statement.

Startel currently has over 210,000 subscribers and has invested up to $97 million in the project since signing a contract with Ericsson in June 1996 to upgrade and expand the existing analogue 800 MHz AMPS network.
Ericsson said with Personal Communication Services, users would be able to use their mobile phones as home phones, office phones and mobile phones, all within the same wireless network.

Digitisation of the network would allow new services to be introduced in Chile including wireless office services for businesses, short messaging services, voice mail, e-mail, and Cellular Digital Packet Data.
